summary:
Jeff Ng opens by noting that building agents has become easy in plumbing terms but they still fail confidently. Six months earlier, building an agent took a team a quarter because three 'taxes' had to be paid first: checkpointing and state persistence (agents are long-lived and stateful while infrastructure is ephemeral, and restarts lose tokens, latency, and risk doubled side effects), sandbox infrastructure for untrusted agent-generated and third-party code, and observability across roughly half a dozen systems. None of these improves what an agent can do.

Cloud providers such as Cloudflare, Vercel, and AWS now ship primitives, and frameworks like Flu, Vercel Eve, and Astra absorb the rest, so defining an agent reduces to a model, instructions or system prompt, tools and skills, and a sandbox. Ng demonstrates this with a small issue-enrichment agent for Linear that, given a ticket about slow time-to-first-character in QA, recommends re-enabling async dispatch. The recommendation is wrong: that setting had just caused an outage and a support engineer had disabled it.

The agent failed because it had no Slack thread or postmortem. Locally, the human acts as the context layer. Once agents run unattended, that human layer disappears and missing context becomes silent failure. Ng proposes a context engine: a system that connects docs, code, tickets, and conversations, models how they relate, reconlicts conflicts, respects access, and delivers a synthesized understanding. MCP is good at access but not understanding. Re-running the same agent against Unblocked's context engine produces the opposite, correct recommendation.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

Defining an agent now reduces to a model, instructions, tools/skills, and a sandbox.
Checkpointing, sandbox isolation, and observability are 'taxes' that improve deployability but not the agent's actual capabilities.

A context engine reconciles docs, code, tickets, and conversations, respects permissions, and delivers synthesized understanding rather than raw results.

sections.title: Intro and the agent construction taxes
sections.summary: Jeff Ng introduces himself as a founding engineer at Unblocked and frames the talk: building agents is now easy but they still get things confidently wrong. Six months ago an agent required a team's quarter of work because of three taxes: checkpointing and state persistence, sandbox infrastructure, and observability across roughly half a dozen systems.

sections.title: How primitives and frameworks remove the plumbing
sections.summary: Cloud infrastructure players (Cloudflare, Vercel, AWS) and frameworks (Flu, Vercel Eve, Astra) have absorbed the taxes. Ng shows that defining an agent now amounts to picking a model, instructions, tools/skills, and a sandbox location, which lets builders focus on the actual logic.

sections.title: Demo: enriching a Linear ticket and the confidently wrong recommendation
sections.summary: Ng demos a small Linear issue-enrichment agent. Given a ticket about QA pipeline latency (hundreds of ms to 3-4s), the agent recommends re-enabling async dispatch. The recommendation is wrong: a support engineer had disabled that setting days earlier because it had caused an outage.

sections.title: Why this does not happen locally
sections.summary: The agent failed because it had the ticket and the repo but not the Slack thread or postmortem. Locally, the human acts as the context layer, asking questions, catching errors, and supplying missing facts on every turn. Once agents run unattended, that layer is gone and missing context becomes silent failure.

sections.title: What a context engine does
sections.summary: Ng defines a context engine as a system that provides task-relevant information, resolves conflicts across datasets, respects access rules, and returns a synthesized understanding. It connects docs, code, tickets, and conversations, builds a model of the organization, and returns reconciled, ranked, scoped context. MCP gives access but not understanding and leaves the agent to reconcile conflicts and flood its context window.

sections.title: The same agent, grounded
sections.summary: Re-running the same Linear ticket through the same agent now augmented with Unblocked's context engine, the system surfaces the postmortem and Slack thread and returns a synthesized summary. The agent's recommendation flips from re-enabling async dispatch (causing an outage) to preventing the recurrence. Ng closes by extending the context-engine idea to coding, code review, customer success, and sales.

demonstrations: Cloudflare + Flu scaffolding shown as minimal agent definition on screen
A Linear ticket about slow time-to-first-character in QA pipeline run through the enrichment agent, which recommended re-enabling async dispatch (the cause of a recent outage)
Re-running the same ticket through the same agent augmented with Unblocked's context engine, which surfaced the postmortem and Slack thread and produced a recommendation to prevent the outage
limitations: MCP floods agents with irrelevant data, fills the context window, and forces the agent to reconcile conflicts ad hoc
Background agents make missing-context errors silently and can misinform teammates and other agents
Local agent usage avoids the context gap only because the human supplies missing facts on every turn
quantitativeClaims: Six months ago building an agent took a team's effort for roughly a quarter
Time to first character in QA pipeline had degraded from hundreds of milliseconds to 3-4 seconds
The outage-causing async-dispatch change had been disabled days before the demo ticket

organization.name: Unblocked
organization.summary: Unblocked is an independent company that builds a context engine for software engineering teams. First-party pages describe a platform that connects source code, messaging, issue trackers, and docs, then injects decision-grade context into AI coding agents and developer questions. The homepage markets Unblocked as the context layer for modern engineering teams, with products including Context Engine, Coding Agents and MCP, Unblocked Code, and AI Code Review. The about page lists Jeffrey Ng on the team and traces the company to founders with Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Apple backgrounds. Flu, Cloudflare, and MCP appear in the talk as agent plumbing, not as the featured organization.
organization.status: Independent company as of the research date. Homepage, about page, context-engine product page, and docs.getunblocked.com are live. No ownership change since the August 2026 talk.
